newsitem.title: PERU: Police arrest three rebel suspects at Peru siege.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest three rebel suspects at Peru siege.

text.p: Peruvian anti-terrorism police said they arrested on Friday three guerrilla suspects outside the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
"We think they were outside looking for information to report back to the national committee" of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), one anti-terrorism police source told Reuters.
The source said the two women and one man, all claiming to be street sellers, were arrested after false identity papers, together with maps and plans, were found in their bags.
Police were prompted to search them after noticing they were behaving "suspiciously," the source added.
Local televison channel America Television showed police bundling the two women into cars before driving them off to anti-terrorism headquarters.
The arrests brought to six the number of people detained outside the residence in recent days on suspicion of being MRTA members, police said.

The MRTA is believed to have various cells in Lima gathering information for the organisation's central committee and seeking to support their 20 comrades still holding 103 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home on the 10th day of the crisis.
Television and radio identified the three arrested on Friday as Jorge Luna, Marlene Vargas and Margot Alvino Jaramillo. Anti-terrorism police did not immediately confirm those names.
